draft.title: The tsar, the tsarina and Rasputin
card: In September 1915 Nicholas II took personal command of the army and left for the front. He was then blamed for Russia's defeats.
Alexandra, the tsarina, was German-born, and many Russians distrusted her during a war with Germany. With Nicholas away, she had a large say in running the government.
Rasputin was a peasant holy man who seemed able to ease the illness of Alexei, the heir. Alexandra trusted him and listened to his advice.

Rumours spread that Rasputin controlled the court and that ministers were being picked and sacked on his word. Many Russians, including nobles, lost respect for the monarchy. Nobles killed Rasputin in December 1916.
draft.remember: With the tsar at the front, Alexandra and Rasputin's influence made the monarchy look weak and out of touch.

a.q: Why did Nicholas II's decision to command the army in 1915 harm his standing?
opts: He became the person blamed for Russia's military defeats
He lost control of the army to the Duma
He gave up the throne to Alexandra while he was away
He was captured by German forces at the front
a.why: As commander, Nicholas was linked directly to the defeats, so blame landed on him. He stayed tsar and was not captured. The Duma did not take control of the army.
a.clue: Think about who gets the blame when the commander's army loses.

b.q: Why did Alexandra's role in government during the war add to distrust of the monarchy?
opts: She was German-born and relied on Rasputin's advice
She was a member of the Duma and opposed the tsar
She was a revolutionary who wanted a republic
She ordered the army to retreat from German forces
b.why: Many Russians distrusted a German-born tsarina in a war with Germany. Her trust in Rasputin fed rumours that he controlled the court. She did not oppose the tsar, sit in the Duma or command the army.
b.clue: Think about her birthplace and the adviser she trusted.

a.best: He became the person blamed for Russia's military defeats

b.best: She was German-born and relied on Rasputin's advice

a.q: Why did Nicholas II's decision to command the army in 1915 harm his standing?
opts: He was tied directly to the army's defeats at the front
He handed control of the army to Rasputin while away
He gave up the throne to Alexandra while he was away

b.q: Why did Alexandra's role in government during the war add to distrust of the monarchy?
opts: She was German-born and relied on Rasputin's advice
She was German-born but left decisions to the ministers
She was British-born and refused to listen to Rasputin
She was Russian-born but sided against Nicholas
b.why: Many Russians distrusted a German-born tsarina in a war with Germany, and her trust in Rasputin fed rumours that he controlled the court. The option saying she left decisions to ministers is tempting because she was German-born, but she had a large say in government and listened to Rasputin.
b.clue: Both parts of the answer must match what the card says about her.
